lines.text: Inform the students that historians outline some basic features that were
common in the early civilizations. These features are: (i) agriculture
(ii) town planning (li) well-organized government (iv) complex religions (v) job
specialization (vi)arts and architecture (vii) public works and (vii) writing.
The world's early civilizations such as Mesopotmia, Egypt, Indus valley and China
developed along the banks of warm rivers.The rivers provided people with a
continuous source of water and fertile soil for domestic use and agricultural activities
such as farming, livestock, and fishing. Agriculture and domestication of animals were
important features of all civilizations. Water tanks, dykes, and small dams were built near
river banks to store water for irrigation of farmlands through water channels.
